scope: Read existing files; write audit/evidence artifacts only. No process inspection, target binary execution, GDI calls, GUI, Hwp, COM, requests, source modification or deployment.

findings.finding: 20% and 25% consume the same snapshot of ctx+0x848 AFTER sub/sup measurement. Snapshot load VA 0x1008e4a4, local store 0x1008e4aa; calls 0x1008e58b and 0x1008e5a2 use IAT 0x100ae2c8 = KERNEL32 MulDiv.

ctx+0x848 stores requested logical input height, written by 0x10084560 at VA 0x1008458d, also 0x100844d0. No direct Roman/GDI TEXTMETRIC substitution at offset call site or in inspected Roman glyph/face setters.
Native character height is returned SIZE.cy from Hnc measurement, distinct from requested size. This permits height-only differences without LAST having changed. Exact target-case cy is unobserved.

rm GPQ should use ASCII G/P/Q after remapping; all exist in HYhwpEQ cmap. Automatic Batang for all Roman letters is unsupported. GlyphExist wrapper behavior/context must still be verified statically before claiming actual runtime face.

Remaining differences may involve node+8 inheritance, measure/cache order, Hnc SIZE.cy mapping/rounding, or style scope. None is established as the cause. No empirical +25/-25 or other patch constant proposed.

evidence.conclusion: Measure lower child then upper child, snapshot ctx+0x848, use the same snapshot for 20% lower and 25% upper offsets. It is the current requested logical font size state, not a GDI TEXTMETRIC value at this call site.
Setter directly writes requested input param_1 to ctx+0x848 and all language heights; width becomes C-truncated param_1/2. No measured-height conversion appears here.
Alternative setter stores height param_1 and width param_2 independently; caller-dependent size changes must not be replaced by global LAST=ss assumptions.

Node preparation inherits node+8 from predecessor/parent reference node+0x60, with a 1000 default if absent. This is a confirmed input-size propagation path; target-case runtime node links are unobserved.
Character height/top come from measurement output SIZE.cy, while LAST/ctx+0x848 is requested size set separately. Web cy(s) is a model assumption, not the native instruction sequence.

rm branch remaps PUA letters to ASCII then checks glyph availability; fallback swaps face for measurement and restores face. Width and cy returned by Hnc wrapper. No ctx+0x848 write in this function body.
Face setter writes language names and ctx+0x858; it does not directly write ctx+0x848. Roman mode alone does not establish Batang fallback.
Fallback depends on GlyphExist (U+00AC forced absent). TTF cmap support is corroboration only, not proof of native wrapper branch.
